schema.description: Attribution tree via each concept's `topic` field; `edges` holds only prereq edges.

node_fields.name: concept name
node_fields.topic: owning topic id; null for topic nodes
node_fields.default_order: default teaching order within the topic

edge_types.prereq: from must be learned before to; strength=hard|soft

nodes.name: Perceptron
nodes.description: The perceptron, a single linear threshold unit computing a weighted sum passed through a step function, the historical building block of neural networks.

nodes.name: Multilayer Perceptron
nodes.description: A multilayer perceptron stacking fully connected layers with nonlinear activations, a universal approximator able to represent complex input-output mappings.

nodes.name: Activation Functions
nodes.description: Activation functions such as ReLU, sigmoid, and tanh introducing nonlinearity between layers, enabling networks to represent non-linear functions.

nodes.name: Forward Propagation
nodes.description: Forward propagation computing a network's output by passing inputs through successive layers, applying weights, biases, and activations stage by stage.

nodes.name: Computational Graphs
nodes.description: A computational graph representing a computation as nodes and edges, enabling automatic differentiation by systematically propagating derivatives.

nodes.name: Backpropagation
nodes.description: Backpropagation computing loss gradients with respect to every parameter by applying the chain rule in reverse through the computational graph.

nodes.name: Loss Functions
nodes.description: Loss functions quantifying prediction error, such as cross-entropy for classification and mean squared error for regression, that guide optimisation.

nodes.name: Stochastic Gradient Descent
nodes.description: Stochastic gradient descent updating network parameters from mini-batch gradient estimates, the core optimisation procedure for training deep networks.

nodes.name: Momentum
nodes.description: Momentum accumulating an exponentially decaying average of past gradients to accelerate descent along consistent directions and dampen oscillation.

nodes.name: Adaptive Optimizers
nodes.description: Adaptive optimisers like Adam and RMSProp scaling per-parameter learning rates from gradient statistics, often speeding and stabilising training.

nodes.name: Learning Rate Schedules
nodes.description: Learning-rate schedules varying the step size during training, such as warmup and decay, to improve convergence speed and final performance.

nodes.name: Vanishing/Exploding Gradients
nodes.description: The vanishing and exploding gradient problem, where gradients shrink or grow across many layers, hampering the training of deep networks.

nodes.name: Weight Initialization
nodes.description: Weight initialisation schemes such as Xavier and He setting initial parameter scales to preserve signal variance and ease optimisation.

nodes.name: Batch Normalization
nodes.description: Batch normalisation standardising layer activations per mini-batch with learnable scale and shift, accelerating and stabilising deep-network training.

nodes.name: Regularization
nodes.description: Regularisation techniques like weight decay and early stopping that constrain model complexity to reduce overfitting and improve generalisation.

nodes.name: Dropout
nodes.description: Dropout randomly deactivating units during training, preventing co-adaptation and acting as an implicit ensemble to improve generalisation.

nodes.name: Convolution
nodes.description: Convolutional layers applying learnable filters across spatial positions, exploiting locality and weight sharing to extract translation-equivariant features.

nodes.name: Padding and Stride
nodes.description: Padding adding border values and stride setting the filter step size, jointly controlling the spatial dimensions of convolutional outputs.

nodes.name: Pooling
nodes.description: Pooling layers downsampling feature maps by summarising local regions with maximum or average operations, reducing resolution and adding invariance.

nodes.name: CNN Architectures
nodes.description: Classic convolutional architectures such as LeNet, AlexNet, and VGG, stacking convolution, activation, and pooling blocks for image recognition.

nodes.name: Residual Networks
nodes.description: Residual networks adding skip connections that let layers learn residual functions, enabling stable training of very deep networks.

nodes.name: Transfer Learning
nodes.description: Transfer learning reusing features from a network pretrained on a large dataset, fine-tuning them for a related task with limited data.

nodes.name: Recurrent Neural Networks
nodes.description: Recurrent neural networks processing sequences by maintaining a hidden state updated at each step and sharing parameters across time.

nodes.name: Backpropagation Through Time
nodes.description: Backpropagation through time unrolling a recurrent network over the sequence and applying backpropagation to compute gradients across time steps.

nodes.name: Long-Range Dependencies
nodes.description: The difficulty recurrent networks face learning long-range dependencies, because gradients vanish or explode when propagated over many time steps.

nodes.name: LSTM
nodes.description: Long short-term memory units using input, forget, and output gates with a cell state to preserve information over long sequences.

nodes.name: GRU
nodes.description: Gated recurrent units, a streamlined gating mechanism with fewer parameters than LSTMs, mitigating vanishing gradients in recurrent models.

nodes.name: Attention Mechanism
nodes.description: Attention mechanisms computing a weighted combination of values, where the weights reflect the relevance of each input to the current query.

nodes.name: Self-Attention
nodes.description: Self-attention relating all positions in a single sequence to one another, letting each element aggregate context from the whole sequence.

nodes.name: Multi-Head Attention
nodes.description: Multi-head attention running several attention operations in parallel subspaces, letting the model jointly attend to different representation aspects.

nodes.name: Positional Encoding
nodes.description: Positional encoding injecting token-order information into otherwise permutation-invariant attention through fixed or learned position representations.

nodes.name: Transformer Architecture
nodes.description: The Transformer, an attention-only encoder-decoder architecture that processes sequences in parallel, underpinning modern language and vision models.

nodes.name: Pretraining & Fine-tuning
nodes.description: Pretraining on large unlabelled corpora with self-supervised objectives, then fine-tuning on downstream tasks, the dominant paradigm for transformers.

nodes.name: Autoencoders
nodes.description: Autoencoders learning compressed representations by training a network to reconstruct its input through a low-dimensional bottleneck.

nodes.name: Variational Autoencoders
nodes.description: Variational autoencoders, probabilistic generative models learning a latent distribution via a variational objective to generate new samples.

nodes.name: Generative Adversarial Networks
nodes.description: Generative adversarial networks pitting a generator against a discriminator in a minimax game, learning to synthesise realistic data.

nodes.name: GAN Training Dynamics
nodes.description: The dynamics and difficulties of training GANs, including instability and mode collapse, addressed by careful loss design and training techniques.

nodes.name: Diffusion Models
nodes.description: Diffusion models generating data by learning to reverse a gradual noising process, denoising random noise into samples step by step.

nodes.name: Normalizing Flows
nodes.description: Normalizing flows transforming a simple base distribution through invertible mappings, enabling exact likelihood evaluation and sampling.
